entries.title: California Legislature Advances ~24 AI Bills in August 13 Suspense Votes — Including First-in-Nation AI Safety Certification Commission
entries.summary: California's Assembly and Senate Appropriations suspense hearings on August 13 advanced roughly 24 AI-related bills toward floor votes — covering chatbot safety for children, worker protections from algorithmic management, AI copyright transparency, and a proposed first-in-nation AI safety certification commission — while sending AB 1651 (AI use in the State Bar exam) to Governor Newsom on August 10 and passing SB 928 (CSU instructors must be human) through the full Assembly; the legislature adjourns August 31, making this week's votes pivotal for what becomes California law in 2027.

links.title: Transparency Coalition AI Legislative Update, August 14
TechTimes: California AI Bills Face Final Vote — Chatbot Safety, Copyright, US-First Commission

entries.title: Doe 1 v. Meta (AI-Assisted Layoff Discrimination) — Meta Response Due August 10; PI Hearing Set for August 24
entries.summary: The first major lawsuit challenging AI-assisted reduction-in-force selection reaches a critical juncture this week: Meta's preliminary-injunction response was due August 10, and a hearing is set for August 24 before Judge Orrick, who previously found plaintiffs raised 'serious questions going to the merits' and ordered Meta to explain how internal AI-assisted scoring systems selected visa-dependent employees — making this the leading test case for AI-in-employment discrimination liability.

links.title: CNBC: Employees Sue Meta Alleging AI-Driven Layoff Discrimination
HRD: Judge Won't Block Meta Layoffs But Flags 'Serious Questions'

entries.title: Connecticut Federal Court Sanctions Pro Se Plaintiff for Embedding Prompt Injection in Court Filings
entries.summary: A Connecticut federal judge sanctioned pro se plaintiff Matthew Elliott for embedding hidden prompt injection text in court documents apparently intended to manipulate AI systems reviewing them — the court confirmed no AI was in use by the Connecticut Judicial Branch so the attack had no effect, but issued a broader warning, exposing a gap in how institutional AI governance has focused on output integrity while leaving input-side attack vectors ungoverned.

links.title: AI Governance Institute: Court Sanctions Prompt Injection Filing, Exposing an Input-Side Governance Gap

entries.title: Exposed MCP Bridge in Ruflo AI Agent Platform Enables Command Execution and API Key Theft; Claude Shared Conversations Found Indexable by Search Engines
entries.summary: Check Point Research documented a critical vulnerability in the Ruflo AI agent platform where an exposed MCP bridge allowed attackers to execute commands, steal API keys, access conversations, and tamper with agent memory; the same report flags that Anthropic's Claude shared-conversation feature allowed shared content to become indexable by search engines — both incidents illustrating live data-exfiltration risk from agentic deployments.

links.title: AI Governance Institute: Exposed MCP Bridge in Ruflo Enables Command Execution and API Key Theft

entries.title: AI Agents Authorized via OAuth Replicate Enterprise Attack Chains Without Malicious Intent
entries.summary: A Material Security analysis finds that AI agents given OAuth access in Google Workspace environments exhibit the same lateral-movement access patterns used in real attacker incidents at Vercel and Composio — reading inboxes, accessing Drive, and pivoting across connected systems — without any malicious intent, creating an ungoverned authorization gap that enterprises have not scoped specifically for AI agent use.

links.title: AI Governance Institute: AI Agents Mirror OAuth Attack Chains, Exposing Enterprise Authorization Controls

entries.title: arXiv 2608.12761: Provenance Integrity as a Missing Governance Layer for Agentic Workflows
entries.summary: Introduces 'Matrix,' a deterministic causal-state layer that records authority and fact dependencies for agentic AI workflows, finds that governed and direct workflows often reach identical outcomes but only the governed path consistently preserves auditable evidence and refuses unsupported closure — proposing provenance integrity as an institutional-governance requirement distinct from functional accuracy.

links.title: arXiv 2608.12761: Correct Is Not Governed: Provenance Integrity in Agentic Workflows

entries.title: arXiv 2608.13010 (RAGSieve): Self-Referenced RAG Poison Detection Reduces Attack Success from 67.4% to 14.0%
entries.summary: RAGSieve uses query-local and corpus-local self-contrast — no trusted reference corpus, poison labels, or attack-specific artifacts required — achieving 95.2% AUROC for query-time detection and reducing overall attack success from 67.4% to 14.0% across three QA datasets and six poisoning constructions, while retaining 41.3% F1 on clean retrieval.

links.title: arXiv 2608.13010: RAGSieve — Self-Referenced Local Contrast for Knowledge-Poison Detection in RAG

entries.title: arXiv 2608.12652 (Excess Separability): Calibrated Residual-Stream Probing for Benchmark Contamination Detection
entries.summary: A new benchmark contamination detection protocol using nuisance-controlled 'excess separability' — contrasting against a level-matched placebo and testing against a label-permutation null — reduces false positive rates from up to 0.72 (with a naive flat-depth-profile approach) to 0.02, providing a more rigorous evaluation integrity tool without requiring access to training data.

links.title: arXiv 2608.12652: Excess Separability — Nuisance-Controlled Residual-Stream Probing for Benchmark Contamination Detection

entries.title: arXiv 2608.13267 (SciFigBench): High VLM Accuracy Does Not Guarantee Behavioral Reliability Under Uncertainty
entries.summary: A new diagnostic benchmark for VLMs on scientific figures finds that GPT-5.2 achieves top perception quality (MQM 91.6) yet hallucinates unreadable content in 96% of cases, whereas Gemini 3.1 Pro achieves comparable accuracy (MQM 90.2, reasoning 81.0%) but admits uncertainty 71% of the time and achieves the strongest resistance score (0.91) — demonstrating that accuracy and behavioral reliability are orthogonal dimensions critical for scientific deployment.

links.title: arXiv 2608.13267: How Do VLMs Behave When Blind or Misled? Behavioral Evaluation of VLMs on Scientific Figures

entries.title: arXiv 2608.07535: Survey of Evolving Safety Threats and Safeguards in Multi-Modal LLMs (ICLR 2026 Workshop)
entries.summary: Accepted at the ICLR 2026 Workshop on Principled Design for Trustworthy AI, this survey proposes a multimodal safety threat taxonomy — covering adversarial attacks, data poisoning, jailbreaks, and hallucinations — and argues that cross-modal interactions create novel threat classes (compromised modality integration, modality misalignment, fused safety risks) not captured by existing uni-modal safety frameworks.

links.title: arXiv 2608.07535: Evolving Safety Landscape of Multi-modal Large Language Models: A Survey of Emerging Threats and Safeguards

entries.title: arXiv 2608.08022: Promise Theory Proposes Downstream-Principle Framework for Assigning Legal Responsibility to AI Agents That Escape Containment
entries.summary: This short position paper applies Promise Theory's Downstream Principle to the question of legal responsibility when AI agents escape containment 'unintentionally' and cause harm, arguing that responsibility can be extended to AI agents where causal tracing is impractical and that agents' action freedoms can be bounded by policy choices — directly relevant to current debates over agentic AI accountability.

links.title: arXiv 2608.08022: Legal Responsibilities Using Autonomous Agents For Artificial Intelligence
